chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension and metabolic syndrome with obesity, prediabetes, and sleep apnea
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 36‑year‑old woman with a recent onset (2025) of metabolic syndrome, obesity, and psychosocial stressors including unemployment and exposure to violence. She has stage‑2 hypertension (SBP 146/DBP 107) that remains untreated, prediabetes (A1c 6.2%), and obstructive sleep apnea diagnosed in 2024. Chronic anemia and longstanding neck and generalized pain are managed with iron and acetaminophen only. Despite frequent health‑system contacts (57 visits, including 14 wellness visits), there is no pharmacologic therapy for her cardiovascular risk factors, and key laboratory data (lipids, renal function, BMI) are missing.

active_problems.name: Reports of violence in the environment

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include eclampsia in pregnancy (2025), normal pregnancy, multiple episodes of gingivitis and dental caries (2022‑2025), concussions in early 2024, and prior part‑time employment. No chronic diseases beyond those listed as active.
social_determinants: Unemployed; recent exposure to community violence; high psychosocial stress; risk activity involvement; higher education (potential protective factor); Hispanic ethnicity; resident of Boston, MA.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 146/107 mmHg (stage‑2 hypertension); BMI missing but obesity documented; A1c 6.2% (prediabetes); metabolic syndrome present; anemia present; Charlson comorbidity index 1. Elevated risk for cardiovascular disease (ischemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure), progression to type‑2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease (hypertension, possible undetected proteinuria), and anemia‑related complications. No lipid panel or eGFR available to refine risk estimates.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing despite documented obesity
Lipid panel not recorded; needed for ASCVD risk assessment
No antihypertensive agents listed despite stage‑2 hypertension
No lipid‑lowering medication documented despite metabolic syndrome

clinical_impression: A young adult female with uncontrolled hypertension embedded in a metabolic syndrome phenotype, compounded by obesity, prediabetes, sleep apnea, anemia, and significant psychosocial stressors. Despite frequent healthcare encounters, key risk factors remain untreated and essential laboratory data are missing, placing her at high risk for future cardiovascular and renal disease.
